title: Demonstrationes circa residua ex divisione potestatum per numeros primos resultantia

deep.reconstruction:
Problem 80 asks for the structure of the residues of fourth powers (biquadrates) modulo a prime P.

Solution. Let a be a primitive root mod P, so the order of a is P−1. Every fourth power x^4 with p∤x is a^{4k}. The biquadratic residues are therefore the terms of the geometric progression 1, a^4, a^8, …. This list is continued until the first exponent 4λ that is divisible by P−1, i.e. 4λ ≡ 0 mod (P−1). Then λ = (P−1)/gcd(4,P−1) is the number of distinct residues. The page treats two cases.

Case I: P = 4n+1. Here P−1 = 4n, so λ = n. The residues are 1, a^4, …, a^{4n−4}, which are n = (P−1)/4 classes.

Case II: P = 4n+3. Here P−1 = 4n+2 and gcd(4,4n+2) = 2, so λ = 2n+1. The progression 1, a^4, …, a^{8n} gives all residues. Since a^{4n+2} ≡ 1, the terms a^{4n+4}, a^{4n+8}, … coincide with a^2, a^6, …. Interleaving them gives 1, a^2, a^4, …, a^{4n}, i.e. all even powers of a. This last conclusion is completed on the next page.

Conclusion: for P ≡ 3 (mod 4), fourth-power residues coincide with quadratic residues; for P ≡ 1 (mod 4) they form the subgroup of index 4. This is the standard description of the image of x ↦ x^4 in the cyclic group (Z/P)^×. The problem serves Euler's programme in E449 of deriving power-residue facts from the existence of primitive roots, after the quadratic and cubic cases.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. 'λ multitudo residuorum' counts nonzero residues only, as is implicit throughout the paper.

In Case II the listed progression stops at a^{8n}, but the interpolated list printed on the next page also runs to a^{8n}. Strictly, the distinct terms are just the 2n+1 even powers up to a^{4n}; the extra terms are redundant, not wrong.

ideas.what: Number of quartic residues mod prime P equals (P−1)/gcd(4,P−1), via a primitive root
ideas.modern_name: Image of the k-th power map in a cyclic group; index gcd(k,p−1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E449; earlier E262/E271 work on power residues); systematized by Gauss, Disquisitiones (1801), arts. 52ff.
ideas.where_published: E449 (Novi Commentarii 18, 1774), Opera omnia I.3; cf. Euler's earlier papers on power residues (E262)

ideas.what: For P ≡ 3 mod 4, biquadratic residues coincide with quadratic residues
ideas.modern_name: x↦x^2 and x↦x^4 have the same image when gcd(4,p−1)=2

deep.surprise_reason: This is a textbook primitive-root computation of quartic residues, published in E449 and well known. The slightly more curious remark about power sums of the four fourth roots appears on the next page, not this one.
transcription_corrections: Transcription is essentially accurate. 'ac residua quaesita orientur quoque' reads as printed (the 'quoque' is Euler's).
'a^{0}' in 'vti a^{0}' is correct as printed.
